hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated, acidified KMnO4 does to every C=C bond, it cleaves it completely to give carbonyls or acids.
Recall the cleavage rule for each C=C carbon: =CH2 gives CO2, =CH- gives a carboxylic acid, and =C with two carbons gives a ketone.
Look for every C=C carbon in beta-carotene that has two carbon groups and no H, then group neighbouring cleavage pieces together to count the product molecules that must contain a ketone.
walkthrough:
**Recall the cleavage rule**

Hot, concentrated, acidified KMnO4 breaks each C=C bond and oxidises each carbon fully. Think simply first.

$$\text{=CH}_2 \to \text{CO}_2, \quad \text{=CHR} \to \text{RCOOH}, \quad \text{=CR}_2 \to \text{R}_2\text{C=O (ketone)}$$

**Count the C=C bonds in beta-carotene**

Notice the structure is symmetrical. There are 2 C=C bonds in the two end rings plus 9 C=C bonds in the long chain.

$$\text{total C=C = 2 + 9 = 11}$$

**Find the =CR2 carbons that make ketones**

Each ring C=C has two $\text{=CR}_2$ carbons, so 4 ketone groups from rings. In the chain, 4 double bonds are $\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)-CH=}$, giving 4 more $\text{=CR}_2$ carbons.

$$\text{ketone-forming carbons = 4 (rings) + 4 (chain) = 8}$$

**Group carbons into real product molecules**

Cleavage does not give single carbons alone. Neighbouring C=C carbons joined by a C-C single bond stay together as one dicarbonyl fragment. The two ketone groups from one ring stay in the same opened-ring molecule.

$$\text{2 ring C=C bonds} \to \text{2 product molecules, each with ketones}$$

**Count ketone-containing fragments**

The left ring fragment plus the left C of double 1 gives molecule 1. The right ring fragment plus the right C of double 1' gives molecule 6. Between them, the four $\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)-}$ units each pair with a neighbouring $\text{=CH-}$ to give 4 more keto-acid fragments.

$$\text{ketone-containing molecules = 2 (ends) + 4 (middle) = 6}$$

options.A: 4 is too low. It counts only part of the ketone sources, for example the 4 chain methyl-substituted carbons, but forgets that the two cyclohexene ring openings also give ketone-containing products.
options.B: 6 is correct. The 2 opened rings give 2 ketone-containing molecules, and the 4 chain C(CH3)= units each end up in a different inter-double fragment with a ketone group, giving 2 + 4 = 6.
options.C: 9 is the number of chain C=C bonds, not the number of ketone products. Most chain double bonds are CH=CH and give only carboxylic acids on cleavage.
options.D: 11 is the total number of C=C bonds cleaved. It is a trap that counts every double bond as a ketone product, ignoring that only =CR2 carbons give ketones.
